A Russian military jet landed in Israel Sunday night, and who was on board is still a mystery.
The aircraft is a Tupolev TU-154, used to fly senior officials and military personnel. It took off from Chkalovsky air base near Moscow and touched down at Ben Gurion Airport around 9 p.m. Flight trackers caught it first. It is expected to depart at noon. No comparable flight has landed in Israel in recent years.
IDF contacts with the Russian military have mostly focused on Russian forces in Syria. Russia thinned out its Syria presence after invading Ukraine and recently began moving forces back to a base near Latakia.
5 days ago, Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, met Putin in Moscow. The U.S.-Iran campaign was among the topics. Russia is set to supply Iran with Sukhoi Su-35 fighter jets.
IDF and Russian Embassy in Israel: "No response."

🇮🇱🇲🇦 Israel expands military footprint in North Africa & opens permanent defense mission in Morocco
Israel is deepening defense ties with Morocco as a delegation led by Defense Ministry Director General Amir Baram met senior Moroccan defense officials on November 10.
Baram is due to inaugurate Israel's permanent Defense Attaché office in Rabat, led by Col. Sharon Itach – the country's first permanent defense attaché to Morocco. Israel is also reportedly seeking to establish military manufacturing facilities inside [the North African kingdom](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/75897).
Israel's expansion of military ties in North Africa and the establishment of a permanent defense mission in Rabat are seen as part of Tel Aviv's methodical efforts to expand its Hexagon Alliance and strengthen its footprint across Africa.
Morocco's neighbor Algeria views Israel's growing presence as[ a security threat](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/74356), while providing support for [the Polisario Front](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73937), which challenges Morocco's claim to[ Western Sahara](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73083). Israel and the US recognized Morocco’s sovereignty over Western Sahara in exchange for Rabat’s normalization of relations with Tel Aviv.
In 2020, Morocco and Israel signed the Abraham Accords, while the cornerstone of their defense ties became the November 2021 Defense Memorandum of Understanding, which:
🌏 marked the first time Israel established a formal defense framework with an Arab nation
🌏 laid the groundwork for direct intelligence sharing and established joint military committees
🌏 opened the door to Israeli defense companies entering the Moroccan market and established a framework for[ industrial cooperation ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76011)
Over the years, Morocco has acquired a wide range of Israeli military equipment through government-to-government contracts. These include:
➡️ The $500 million Barak MX air and missile defense system (2022)
➡️ A $1 billion, five-year contract to replace existing Airbus and Thales space-based surveillance systems with Israel's Ofek-13 spy satellites (2024)
➡️ A $200 million contract for 36 Atmos 2000 self-propelled artillery systems manufactured by Elbit Systems (2025)
➡️ Israeli-made drones, including Elbit Systems' Hermes 450 and Hermes 900, as well as IAI's Heron 1.

events.text:
🇺🇸🇨🇳 US Marines risk isolation and paralysis in any western Pacific clash with China, officers warn
Forward-deployed US Marines along the first island chain could find themselves cut off, immobile and short of supplies if conflict erupts with China, according to assessments by a retired three-star general and a serving lieutenant colonel.
China’s anti-access/area-denial systems and precision strike networks could turn dispersed Marine units into fixed targets rather than a maneuver force, argue retired Lt. Gen. Stephen Sklenka and Lt. Col. Merritt Mitchell, writing separately in the US Naval Institute’s Proceedings.
Sklenka argues that:
🔴 mobilization would have to occur from bases under simultaneous cyber and missile attack 
🔴 force closure would take place at the edge of contested zones rather than secure ports or airfields
🔴 marines would need to sustain themselves for up to 75 days without traditional air or sea superiority 
🔴 if reinforcements cannot punch through, Marines already positioned along the first island chain risk being left to fight an isolated, terminal engagement
Mitchell focuses on the political and operational constraints of the stand-in force:
🔴 detection increasingly equals destruction: units that cannot reposition faster than Chinese retargeting cycles become fixed targets
🔴 many potential operating sites lie in allied territory where governments may withhold permission for offensive operations
🔴 without those permissions in place before crisis, the stand-in force cannot maneuver when it matters
